title: In-Context Impersonation Reveals Large Language Models’ Strengths and Biases
findings: When impersonating a 'World Religions expert', the language model's performance on the World Religions task from the MMLU benchmark was significantly higher compared to when it impersonated other domain experts or non-domain experts. This suggests that in-context impersonation of a relevant expert can effectively enhance a model's specialized knowledge recall and reasoning.
